trials.name: CNS and Plasma Amyloid-Beta Kinetics in AD
trials.drug: Stable Isotope Labeling Kinetics / Plasma Aβ (Diagnostic method)
trials.population: Adults age 60 and older from the Alzheimer's Disease Research Center with known amyloid status
trials.primary_endpoint: Analysis of SILK blood and CSF Aβ isoforms comparing amyloid positive group with control group
trials.results_summary: Confirmed that plasma Aβ turnover kinetics are significantly faster than in CSF. Demonstrated that the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio drops in amyloid-positive patients, validating plasma Aβ ratios as an accurate screening mechanism for CNS amyloidosis.

trials.name: QUIP I
trials.drug: PrecivityAD blood test (Plasma Aβ42/40 ratio & ApoE)
trials.population: Memory Specialists and their patients presenting with mild cognitive impairment or early dementia
trials.primary_endpoint: Evaluate patient selection and score interpretation through clinician survey responses
trials.results_summary: Revealed that providing physicians with the PrecivityAD blood test results significantly influenced clinical decision-making, increasing diagnostic confidence and altering patient management plans.

trials.name: ADELAIDE
trials.population: Patients aged 50+ with symptoms of MCI or cognitive impairment
trials.primary_endpoint: Time to achieve >=90% Diagnostic Confidence for AD or Non-AD

related_evidence.description: Validation study demonstrating that high-precision plasma Aβ42/40 accurately predicts current and future brain amyloidosis.
Large-scale multi-cohort validation (ADNI, BioFINDER) of Plasma Amyloid-β 42/40 for detecting AD amyloid plaques.
Peer-reviewed results from the QUIP I trial showing the real-world clinical impact of the PrecivityAD test.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence supporting the diagnostic utility of plasma Aβ concentrations (specifically the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio) is exceptionally strong and has transitioned smoothly into commercial clinical practice. The foundational kinetic study in Ovod et al. (NCT02021682) elegantly explained the brain-to-blood transport differences seen in Alzheimer's disease. While the initial study was limited by a small sample size (N=41) and retrospective amyloid-status anchoring, its core findings have been subsequently validated in massive, independent cohorts worldwide, demonstrating highly robust diagnostic accuracy (AUCs routinely > 0.85). The assay was commercialized by C2N Diagnostics as the PrecivityAD test; clinical utility data from subsequent registry trials (e.g., QUIP I) confirms that these blood biomarkers reliably alter physician diagnostic confidence and patient management.
discrepancies: The document states a study population size of 41 participants, but the foundational registry record (NCT02021682) shows an actual total enrollment of 58.

The document does not list any trial registration number, but the study matches NCT02021682 perfectly (supported by the shared R01NS065667 grant, principal investigator, and unique SILK pulse-labeling methodology).
